    private bindRun() {
        const boundRunId = this.bindingStore.getSnapshot()
        if (this.subscribedRunId === boundRunId) return

        this.unsubscribeRun?.()
        this.subscribedRunId = boundRunId
        this.unsubscribeRun = boundRunId
            ? this.runRegistry.subscribeRun(boundRunId, this.handleRunChange)
            : null
    }

    private updateFromSources() {
        const boundRunId = this.bindingStore.getSnapshot()
        const run = boundRunId ? this.runRegistry.getRunStore(boundRunId)?.getSnapshot() ?? null : null
        const selectedConversation = this.conversationStore.getSnapshot().selectedConversation
        const pendingRunConversation = !!boundRunId && !run?.conversation
        const resolvedConversation = resolveDisplayedConversation(run?.conversation ?? null, selectedConversation)
        const conversation = pendingRunConversation && !selectedConversation
            ? this.conversation
            : resolvedConversation
        const status = pendingRunConversation && !selectedConversation && this.conversation
            ? this.status
            : displayedStatus(run, selectedConversation)
        const displayingLiveConversation = !selectedConversation
            || !run?.conversation
            || selectedConversation.id === run.conversation.id
        const queuedPrompts = displayingLiveConversation ? run?.queuedPrompts ?? EMPTY_QUEUED_PROMPTS : EMPTY_QUEUED_PROMPTS
        const runId = displayingLiveConversation ? run?.runId ?? null : null
        const change = displayingLiveConversation ? run?.conversationChange ?? null : null

        const submissions = displayingLiveConversation
            ? this.conversationStore.getSubmissions().filter((submission) => (
                submission.runId === boundRunId
                && submission.selectionId === (selectedConversation?.id ?? null)
            ))
            : EMPTY_SUBMISSIONS
        const acceptedPrompts = submissions
            .filter((submission) => submission.state === 'queued'
                && !!submission.prompt
                && !queuedPrompts.some(({ id }) => id === submission.prompt?.id))
            .map((submission) => submission.prompt as ActionQueuedPrompt)
        const displayedQueuedPrompts = acceptedPrompts.length > 0

        const pendingRows = submissions.filter((submission) => submission.state !== 'queued')

        this.applyConversation(conversation, change, status, displayedQueuedPrompts, runId)
        this.publishSubmissions(pendingRows)
    }

“Live run” means the conversation attached to the currently running agent process. A historical conversation is one selected from saved history. The popup can show either: when `selectedConversation` is set, it shows that selection; when it is cleared, it shows the bound run’s conversation. That is what `showLiveRun()` does. [Conversation store](C:/Users/janbo/Documents/dev/md2_workers/dev3/app/src/components/actions/conversation/state/action_conversation_store.ts:55)

The switch happens in the start callback because a new or restarted run does not have a run ID when Send is pressed. Once the backend supplies the ID, the popup binds to that run and clears the old history selection so the user sees the conversation they just started. [Start callback](C:/Users/janbo/Documents/dev/md2_workers/dev3/app/src/components/actions/run/popup/action_popup_operations.ts:125)

My earlier finding is **already addressed in the current code**: the callback records the selected conversation and bound run at submission time, then switches only if both are still the same when the run starts. If the user has selected another conversation meanwhile, it leaves that selection alone. I should have checked the updated code before presenting that finding as outstanding.

You’re right that a historical conversation and a running conversation are the **same kind of conversation**. I described them as if they were different domain objects, which was misleading.

The distinction is whether a **run is currently attached** to the conversation. A saved `AgentConversation` has an `id`, entries, and a persistence path; it has no `runId` field. The run ID identifies an execution. To pick up a saved conversation, the app passes its path as `continueFrom`, loads that conversation, and starts a run attached to it. [Conversation type](C:/Users/janbo/Documents/dev/md2_workers/dev3/app/src/data/data_types.ts:398) · [Continuation](C:/Users/janbo/Documents/dev/md2_workers/dev3/desktop/src/actions/action/action_agent_executor.js:46)

So “show live run” is a UI instruction: display the conversation attached to the newly started run instead of the previously selected saved view. The switch waits for the start callback because that is when the new run ID becomes available. The conversation itself has not changed into a different kind of object.

> display the conversation attached to the newly started run instead of the previously selected saved view.

* a user can only continue a previous conversation if it was selected. we know the conversation id, when an input is sent, it should also include the conversation id to link stuff together, right?
* once a run has been created and the run-id is known, the electron app just needs to report: conversation id x now attached to run-id y, right?
* no objects should be replaced at all.
* so `display the conversation attached to the newly started run instead of the previously selected saved view` 
  * here: previously selected saved view has to be the same as conversation attached to the newly started run
  * we should not force any view upon the user. if he still has the conversation open, good, if he switched, then that is ok also, we should not force it back

so, is there any other technical reason why it is currently done the way you describe or is this just a made-up rule? are there any technicial restrictions to do it the way I described?

[Continuation loading](C:/Users/janbo/Documents/dev/md2_workers/dev3/desktop/src/actions/action/action_agent_executor.js:46) · [Conversation ID reuse](C:/Users/janbo/Documents/dev/md2_workers/dev3/desktop/src/actions/agent/agent_runner_service.js:130)

There is **no technical requirement to force the view back**. In fact, the display resolver already uses live updates when the selected conversation ID matches the run’s conversation ID, while allowing a different selection to remain visible. [Display resolver](C:/Users/janbo/Documents/dev/md2_workers/dev3/app/src/components/actions/conversation/state/action_conversation_store.ts:55)

The current `showLiveRun()` call compensates for an implementation detail: temporary submissions are rebound with `selectionId: null`, and the chatlog filters them by the current selection ID. If the saved conversation stays selected, that temporary row can disappear. [Submission binding](C:/Users/janbo/Documents/dev/md2_workers/dev3/app/src/components/actions/conversation/state/action_conversation_store.ts:156) · [Chatlog filter](C:/Users/janbo/Documents/dev/md2_workers/dev3/app/src/components/actions/conversation/transcript/action_conversation_chatlog_tracker.ts:343)

The appropriate design is to associate the submission with the conversation ID and new run ID, then derive what to show from the user’s current selection. Switching the user’s selection is unnecessary.

You’re right; “rebound” was my wording, and it obscured what the code does.

A **temporary submission** is the local chat row created immediately when you press Send, before Electron has confirmed the prompt. It can remain while the app waits for a queued prompt or sent user message.

That row **does not currently store a conversation ID**. It stores a `runId` (initially `null` when starting a run) and a `selectionId`, which is a copy of whichever conversation ID was selected when Send was pressed. When Electron returns the new run ID, `bindSubmission()` assigns it to the row and sets `selectionId` to `null`. [Submission creation and binding](C:/Users/janbo/Documents/dev/md2_workers/dev3/app/src/components/actions/conversation/state/action_conversation_store.ts:131)

So your objection is valid: `selectionId` is being used as a proxy for conversation identity and display state, even though those are different things. That is why my explanation sounded unnatural. The temporary submission should identify its conversation directly; the current code does not.

You’re right about the model. I kept explaining the current implementation as though it were a requirement.

The React app can generate a conversation ID before sending the first prompt and pass it to Electron. For a continued conversation, it already knows the ID. A temporary row can then belong to **conversation ID + local submission ID** from the moment it is created. The run ID belongs to the execution and can be tracked separately by the service for routing backend events; it does not need to be stored on each row.

That is **not how this code currently works**: new conversations get their ID through the backend reservation path, and temporary rows carry run and selection IDs. Changing to your model requires changing that start protocol and the frontend event correlation. I found no inherent technical restriction that requires the current approach.

Yes, that can work. A unique local submission ID is enough to match an acknowledgement to a submission. The conversation ID and run ID can live on the **owning conversation/run state**, rather than on every row.

Two details matter:

- **Before acknowledgement**, the UI still needs to know which open conversation should show the row. Keeping submissions in a list owned by that conversation solves this; the row itself needs no conversation ID.
- **After acknowledgement**, later queue and sent-message events must remain traceable to the same submission. Electron must echo the local ID in those events, or return a queue/message ID that the frontend maps to it. Otherwise rapid identical prompts can be matched to the wrong row.

The current bridge does not yet provide that protocol: `startAction` returns only a run ID, and `enqueueActionPrompt` takes only run ID and text; its events have no local submission ID. [Bridge contract](C:/Users/janbo/Documents/dev/md2_workers/dev3/app/src/data/electron_action_bridge.ts:179) · [Event types](C:/Users/janbo/Documents/dev/md2_workers/dev3/app/src/data/action_run_types.ts:169)

So there is no conceptual obstacle. It requires carrying the submission ID through the request, acknowledgement, and relevant events, including rejection, with event ordering handled if an event arrives before the acknowledgement.
ok, fix it like we discussed

I’ll update the submission flow so a local submission ID follows each request through Electron’s acknowledgement and events, while conversation and run ownership stay in the service. I’ll first map the bridge and backend call sites, then change the code and run focused tests and lint.

# Architectural decisions

Project-wide decisions for MDÂ². The app is a Vite React web app in `app/`; `desktop/` is a separate Electron host that can load the website and expose local capabilities through preload bridges.

## File naming

| Decision | Rule | Rationale |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Code files use lowercase snake_case names. | All code files in `app/src/` and `desktop/` use lowercase words separated by underscores, for example `github_auth_service.ts`, `project_workspace.tsx`, and `local_git_service.js`. Test files keep the same base name with `.test` before the extension, for example `github_auth_service.test.ts`. Exported symbols keep normal TypeScript/JavaScript casing such as `GithubAuthService`, `ProjectWorkspace`, and `useGithubAuth`. | A single file naming convention avoids mixed PascalCase, camelCase, and hyphenated filenames, and keeps imports predictable across Windows and case-sensitive environments. |

## Services and state

| Decision | Rule | Rationale |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Global singleton services own domain state and logic. | Each domain is a class in `src/services/**`, instantiated once at module level and exported, for example `export const indexesService = new IndexesService()`. React components do not own domain state. | Keeps business logic out of components, testable without a DOM, and shared across windows/views without Redux, Zustand, or Context stores. |
| Service location follows usage scope. | If a service is specific to one UI element and used only there, place it beside that component. Generic or shared services, such as logging, database access, config, storage, or cross-screen domain logic, belong in `src/services/`. | Keeps component-owned behavior local while preserving `src/services/` for reusable application services. |
| Consumers use direct imports or the service injector. | Direct import when no import cycle exists; use `src/services/service_injector.js` when a cycle would occur. Every global singleton service registers itself in its constructor with `inj.register('myService', this)`. | The service graph is dense; the injector is a bare global registry that defers resolution to call time. |
| Services have a two-phase lifecycle. | Constructors only register and set unloaded state such as `null`. Config-dependent or service-dependent work runs in `init()`, `start()`, app bootstrap (`App.jsx`), or a `loaded` lifecycle event. `configService.config` is private; callers use `get`, `set`, and `clear`. | Module evaluation order is not guaranteed, so `configService` is not usable at import time. Reading config in a constructor is a bug. |

## Card state

| Decision | Rule | Rationale |
| --- | --- | --- |
| The application has one `Card` domain type. | Do not create separate canonical, project, snapshot, or editor card types. The card-owning service holds the loaded cards and exposes focused operations that change only the requested field. React snapshots and editor drafts are read values; they must never replace or merge a complete card. Parser bookkeeping may remain private persistence metadata, but it is not another card model. | One card concept gives state a clear owner and prevents stale copies from overwriting newer worktree, activity, ordering, policy, or body values. |
| Card UI subscribes at field level. | A component subscribes only to the primitive or stable reference it renders, using granular `EventTarget` events and `useSyncExternalStore`. Do not clone or stringify a complete card to detect a field change. Group fields only in a deliberately small, stable projection when they are always rendered together. | A one-field change allocates and rerenders only what consumes that field, keeping memory use bounded and the UI responsive. |
| Cards are serialized only at persistence boundaries. | Mutate the owned `Card` through a focused operation, then serialize its current state when the persistence batch flushes. Editor changes update only the edited field. Activity linking updates only activity references. External file changes are parsed and applied deliberately without replacing dirty local state. | Persistence remains deterministic while concurrent saves and external updates cannot discard unrelated newer values. |


## Events and React integration

| Decision | Rule | Rationale |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Services notify observers through their own `EventTarget`. | Services expose an `EventTarget` and dispatch named `CustomEvent` domain events such as `activeIndex`, `added`, `deleted`, or `changedBox`. Observers subscribe with `addEventListener` and unsubscribe with `removeEventListener` on the owning service. | Decouples producers from consumers without depending on Node `EventEmitter`, which is not available in the browser-first React app. |
| Custom hooks bridge service events to functional components. | Hooks in `src/components/hooks/`, such as `useActiveIndex` and `useProjectConfig`, seed `useState` from a service property, subscribe in `useEffect`, unsubscribe in cleanup, and return the value. Prefer hook + service over prop chains. | Components stay declarative and avoid direct event plumbing. |
| Components subscribe at the smallest rendering boundary. | Root and layout components compose UI regions and pass structural inputs. Components that render changing application data subscribe through hooks themselves. Do not hoist changing data into ancestors only to pass it downward. | Limits rerenders to affected UI, protects transient state such as open popups, and avoids broad prop chains. |
| Components use the app theme service path. | `App` owns theme mode through `useThemeMode()`, builds the MUI theme with `createAppTheme(mode)`, and provides it through `ThemeProvider`. Components read theme values with MUI APIs such as `useTheme`, `useMediaQuery`, and `sx`; only controls that change the palette mode receive `mode` and `onToggleTheme`. | Theme state, persistence, and palette construction stay centralized while components remain presentation-focused. |

const boundRunId = this.bindingStore.getSnapshot()
        const run = boundRunId ? this.runRegistry.getRunStore(boundRunId)?.getSnapshot() ?? null : null
        const selectedConversation = this.conversationStore.getSnapshot().selectedConversation
        const pendingRunConversation = !!boundRunId && !run?.conversation
        const resolvedConversation = resolveDisplayedConversation(run?.conversation ?? null, selectedConversation)
        const conversation = pendingRunConversation && !selectedConversation
            ? this.conversation
            : resolvedConversation
        const status = pendingRunConversation && !selectedConversation && this.conversation
            ? this.status
            : displayedStatus(run, selectedConversation)
        const displayingLiveConversation = !selectedConversation
            || !run?.conversation
            || selectedConversation.id === run.conversation.id
        const queuedPrompts = displayingLiveConversation ? run?.queuedPrompts ?? EMPTY_QUEUED_PROMPTS : EMPTY_QUEUED_PROMPTS
        const runId = displayingLiveConversation ? run?.runId ?? null : null
        const change = displayingLiveConversation ? run?.conversationChange ?? null : null

        const submissions = displayingLiveConversation
            ? this.conversationStore.getSubmissions().filter((submission) => (
                submission.runId === boundRunId
                && submission.selectionId === (selectedConversation?.id ?? null)
            ))
            : EMPTY_SUBMISSIONS
        const acceptedPrompts = submissions
            .filter((submission) => submission.state === 'queued'
                && !!submission.prompt
                && !queuedPrompts.some(({ id }) => id === submission.prompt?.id))
            .map((submission) => submission.prompt as ActionQueuedPrompt)
        const displayedQueuedPrompts = acceptedPrompts.length > 0
            ? [...queuedPrompts, ...acceptedPrompts]
            : queuedPrompts
        const pendingRows = submissions.filter((submission) => submission.state !== 'queued')

        this.applyConversation(conversation, change, status, displayedQueuedPrompts, runId)
        this.publishSubmissions(pendingRows)
    }

    private applyConversation(

        tracker.getSubmissions,
        tracker.getSubmissions,

    return submissions.map((submission) => <ActionPendingSubmissionRow key={submission.id} submission={submission} />)

We generated a squence diagram (json file), of the action popup and its interactions. There, you can see that input sent by the user to the agent, first goes to backend and back to frontend before it is shown in the chatlog. This is too late.

How it should work: 

* User sends input
* Prompt is immediatly shown in chatlog, but as an Â´in transmissionÂ´ text.
* Once the frontend gets the prompt back from backend, we show text as we do now, sent.

## Current state

`runPopupAction` reads the editor draft. For an active agent run, it waits for `enqueueActionPrompt` to return before clearing the draft. The desktop backend validates the prompt, returns a queued entry, and publishes `agentPromptQueued`; `ActionRunRegistry` then exposes it as a `Queued` row in the chatlog. When the agent accepts the prompt, `agentUserMessage` adds the normal sent message. For a new or restarted run, the chatlog likewise waits for backend run events before showing the user message. The submit action itself creates no chatlog row.

## implementation details

* On Send or the keyboard shortcut, capture the exact submitted editor text and add a temporary chatlog row marked `In transmission` immediately, before awaiting the bridge. Apply this to new, restarted, and active agent runs. Keep temporary submission data in a service owned by the popup action/context, and render it through the chatlog tracker; do not insert it into `AgentConversation.entries` or persist it.
* Scope each temporary row to the submitted action, card identity (`cardInternalId`) or project context, and conversation/run binding. Keep a local submission ID so identical prompts and rapid submissions stay distinct. Paths identify persistence locations, not the submission's domain identity.
* Reconcile each temporary row with its corresponding backend update: replace it with the existing `Queued` row when `agentPromptQueued` arrives, or with the normal sent user message when `agentUserMessage` arrives. Match submissions by run and submission order, not prompt text; the bridge response supplies the backend queue ID for later queue updates. Keep an accepted row visible when `agentPromptRemoved` precedes `agentUserMessage`, until the sent message replaces it. Handle events arriving before the bridge promise resolves without duplicates.
* If submission fails before backend acceptance, remove only that temporary row, retain or restore its editor text without overwriting newer edits, and report the error through `dialogService`. Clear temporary rows when their run ends without accepting them, or when the popup action/context changes. Historical conversations must never show another run's temporary rows.
* Cover immediate display, queue and user-message reconciliation, new and restarted runs, duplicate prompt text, backend rejection, newer editor edits, and historical selection in focused service and popup/chatlog tests.

## acceptance criteria

* Pressing Send or Ctrl/Cmd+Enter shows submitted text in the chatlog as `In transmission` before the backend responds, for new, restarted, and active agent runs.
* Backend queue acceptance replaces the temporary row with one `Queued` row; agent acceptance replaces it with one normal sent user message. No duplicate row appears if events and bridge response arrive in either order.
* Failed submission removes the temporary row, preserves unsent text, and shows an error. Later editor changes remain intact.
* Rapid or identical submissions each reconcile with their own backend result. Switching to a historical conversation hides pending rows from the live run.
* Temporary rows never enter persisted conversations. Existing queued-prompt editing and deletion still work after backend acceptance.

# Architectural decisions

Project-wide decisions for MDÂ². The app is a Vite React web app in `app/`; `desktop/` is a separate Electron host that can load the website and expose local capabilities through preload bridges.

## File naming

| Decision | Rule | Rationale |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Code files use lowercase snake_case names. | All code files in `app/src/` and `desktop/` use lowercase words separated by underscores, for example `github_auth_service.ts`, `project_workspace.tsx`, and `local_git_service.js`. Test files keep the same base name with `.test` before the extension, for example `github_auth_service.test.ts`. Exported symbols keep normal TypeScript/JavaScript casing such as `GithubAuthService`, `ProjectWorkspace`, and `useGithubAuth`. | A single file naming convention avoids mixed PascalCase, camelCase, and hyphenated filenames, and keeps imports predictable across Windows and case-sensitive environments. |

## Services and state

| Decision | Rule | Rationale |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Global singleton services own domain state and logic. | Each domain is a class in `src/services/**`, instantiated once at module level and exported, for example `export const indexesService = new IndexesService()`. React components do not own domain state. | Keeps business logic out of components, testable without a DOM, and shared across windows/views without Redux, Zustand, or Context stores. |
| Service location follows usage scope. | If a service is specific to one UI element and used only there, place it beside that component. Generic or shared services, such as logging, database access, config, storage, or cross-screen domain logic, belong in `src/services/`. | Keeps component-owned behavior local while preserving `src/services/` for reusable application services. |
| Consumers use direct imports or the service injector. | Direct import when no import cycle exists; use `src/services/service_injector.js` when a cycle would occur. Every global singleton service registers itself in its constructor with `inj.register('myService', this)`. | The service graph is dense; the injector is a bare global registry that defers resolution to call time. |
| Services have a two-phase lifecycle. | Constructors only register and set unloaded state such as `null`. Config-dependent or service-dependent work runs in `init()`, `start()`, app bootstrap (`App.jsx`), or a `loaded` lifecycle event. `configService.config` is private; callers use `get`, `set`, and `clear`. | Module evaluation order is not guaranteed, so `configService` is not usable at import time. Reading config in a constructor is a bug. |

## Card state

| Decision | Rule | Rationale |
| --- | --- | --- |
| The application has one `Card` domain type. | Do not create separate canonical, project, snapshot, or editor card types. The card-owning service holds the loaded cards and exposes focused operations that change only the requested field. React snapshots and editor drafts are read values; they must never replace or merge a complete card. Parser bookkeeping may remain private persistence metadata, but it is not another card model. | One card concept gives state a clear owner and prevents stale copies from overwriting newer worktree, activity, ordering, policy, or body values. |
| Card UI subscribes at field level. | A component subscribes only to the primitive or stable reference it renders, using granular `EventTarget` events and `useSyncExternalStore`. Do not clone or stringify a complete card to detect a field change. Group fields only in a deliberately small, stable projection when they are always rendered together. | A one-field change allocates and rerenders only what consumes that field, keeping memory use bounded and the UI responsive. |
| Cards are serialized only at persistence boundaries. | Mutate the owned `Card` through a focused operation, then serialize its current state when the persistence batch flushes. Editor changes update only the edited field. Activity linking updates only activity references. External file changes are parsed and applied deliberately without replacing dirty local state. | Persistence remains deterministic while concurrent saves and external updates cannot discard unrelated newer values. |


## Events and React integration

| Decision | Rule | Rationale |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Services notify observers through their own `EventTarget`. | Services expose an `EventTarget` and dispatch named `CustomEvent` domain events such as `activeIndex`, `added`, `deleted`, or `changedBox`. Observers subscribe with `addEventListener` and unsubscribe with `removeEventListener` on the owning service. | Decouples producers from consumers without depending on Node `EventEmitter`, which is not available in the browser-first React app. |
| Custom hooks bridge service events to functional components. | Hooks in `src/components/hooks/`, such as `useActiveIndex` and `useProjectConfig`, seed `useState` from a service property, subscribe in `useEffect`, unsubscribe in cleanup, and return the value. Prefer hook + service over prop chains. | Components stay declarative and avoid direct event plumbing. |
| Components subscribe at the smallest rendering boundary. | Root and layout components compose UI regions and pass structural inputs. Components that render changing application data subscribe through hooks themselves. Do not hoist changing data into ancestors only to pass it downward. | Limits rerenders to affected UI, protects transient state such as open popups, and avoids broad prop chains. |
| Components use the app theme service path. | `App` owns theme mode through `useThemeMode()`, builds the MUI theme with `createAppTheme(mode)`, and provides it through `ThemeProvider`. Components read theme values with MUI APIs such as `useTheme`, `useMediaQuery`, and `sx`; only controls that change the palette mode receive `mode` and `onToggleTheme`. | Theme state, persistence, and palette construction stay centralized while components remain presentation-focused. |

I found four implementation issues. The temporary rows stay out of persisted conversations, but reconciliation and draft handling are not fully correct.

- **A rejected rapid submission can lose its text.** If two sends use the same editor revision, the first successful response clears the draft. If the second response then fails, its temporary row disappears and the draft remains empty. [Send handling](/C:/Users/janbo/Documents/dev/md2_workers/dev3/app/src/components/actions/run/popup/action_popup_operations.ts:225). **Fix:** Track draft ownership per submission and restore a rejected submission only when the editor has not acquired newer text.

- **Starting a run overrides a newer history selection.** While a new or restarted run is starting, the user can select a historical conversation. The start callback unconditionally calls `showLiveRun()`, switching the display back to the live run. [Start callback](/C:/Users/janbo/Documents/dev/md2_workers/dev3/app/src/components/actions/run/popup/action_popup_operations.ts:143). **Fix:** Record the selection at submission time and switch to the live run only if the user has not changed it.

- **A failed new run can discard an unaccepted prompt.** The start callback clears the draft as soon as it receives a run ID, but prompt restoration after a failed result is limited to restarted runs. If a new run fails before recording the user message, the temporary row and draft are both lost. [Failure handling](/C:/Users/janbo/Documents/dev/md2_workers/dev3/app/src/components/actions/run/popup/action_popup_operations.ts:166). **Fix:** Apply the same acceptance check and guarded draft restoration to new runs.

- **Deletion in another popup leaves a false pending row.** Every `agentPromptRemoved` event marks the submission as awaiting a sent message. Only deletion through this popup’s button removes that row; deletion elsewhere leaves it visible and a later user message can remove the wrong submission. [Event reconciliation](/C:/Users/janbo/Documents/dev/md2_workers/dev3/app/src/components/actions/conversation/state/action_conversation_store.ts:232). **Fix:** Have the backend distinguish dispatch from deletion in the removal event, then retain a temporary row only for dispatch.

ok, we fixed `A rejected rapid submission can lose its text.` the drafts are now linked to the 'conversation id and get cleared as soon as the draft gets send for no other reason.

we also fixed`Starting a run overrides a newer history selection` :

> Temporary rows now carry a local submission ID; the service keeps their conversation and run association. Electron carries that ID through queued-prompt and sent-message events, so identical rapid prompts reconcile individually. New conversations receive an ID before Send, and starting a run no longer changes the user’s conversation selection.



next: `A failed new run can discard an unaccepted prompt.`

> If a new run fails before recording the user message, the temporary row and draft are both lost.

that should not be possible, recording the new user message should be synchronously executed with starting the run. is this really a problem or did you just make this up

We generated a squence diagram (json file), of the action popup and its interactions. There, you can see that input sent by the user to the agent, first goes to backend and back to frontend before it is shown in the chatlog. This is too late.

How it should work: 

* User sends input
* Prompt is immediatly shown in chatlog, but as an Â´in transmissionÂ´ text.
* Once the frontend gets the prompt back from backend, we show text as we do now, sent.

## Current state

`runPopupAction` reads the editor draft. For an active agent run, it waits for `enqueueActionPrompt` to return before clearing the draft. The desktop backend validates the prompt, returns a queued entry, and publishes `agentPromptQueued`; `ActionRunRegistry` then exposes it as a `Queued` row in the chatlog. When the agent accepts the prompt, `agentUserMessage` adds the normal sent message. For a new or restarted run, the chatlog likewise waits for backend run events before showing the user message. The submit action itself creates no chatlog row.

## implementation details

* On Send or the keyboard shortcut, capture the exact submitted editor text and add a temporary chatlog row marked `In transmission` immediately, before awaiting the bridge. Apply this to new, restarted, and active agent runs. Keep temporary submission data in a service owned by the popup action/context, and render it through the chatlog tracker; do not insert it into `AgentConversation.entries` or persist it.
* Scope each temporary row to the submitted action, card identity (`cardInternalId`) or project context, and conversation/run binding. Keep a local submission ID so identical prompts and rapid submissions stay distinct. Paths identify persistence locations, not the submission's domain identity.
* Reconcile each temporary row with its corresponding backend update: replace it with the existing `Queued` row when `agentPromptQueued` arrives, or with the normal sent user message when `agentUserMessage` arrives. Match submissions by run and submission order, not prompt text; the bridge response supplies the backend queue ID for later queue updates. Keep an accepted row visible when `agentPromptRemoved` precedes `agentUserMessage`, until the sent message replaces it. Handle events arriving before the bridge promise resolves without duplicates.
* If submission fails before backend acceptance, remove only that temporary row, retain or restore its editor text without overwriting newer edits, and report the error through `dialogService`. Clear temporary rows when their run ends without accepting them, or when the popup action/context changes. Historical conversations must never show another run's temporary rows.
* Cover immediate display, queue and user-message reconciliation, new and restarted runs, duplicate prompt text, backend rejection, newer editor edits, and historical selection in focused service and popup/chatlog tests.

## acceptance criteria

* Pressing Send or Ctrl/Cmd+Enter shows submitted text in the chatlog as `In transmission` before the backend responds, for new, restarted, and active agent runs.
* Backend queue acceptance replaces the temporary row with one `Queued` row; agent acceptance replaces it with one normal sent user message. No duplicate row appears if events and bridge response arrive in either order.
* Failed submission removes the temporary row, preserves unsent text, and shows an error. Later editor changes remain intact.
* Rapid or identical submissions each reconcile with their own backend result. Switching to a historical conversation hides pending rows from the live run.
* Temporary rows never enter persisted conversations. Existing queued-prompt editing and deletion still work after backend acceptance.

You’re right that the backend adds the user message to the conversation before launching the agent. My earlier wording was too broad: **a failed new run does not necessarily lose its prompt**.

The narrower failure is real. The action runner returns a run ID before the agent starts ([action_runner_service.js](/C:/Users/janbo/Documents/dev/md2_workers/dev3/desktop/src/actions/action/action_runner_service.js:199)). Agent startup then adds the message in memory, but executable lookup and checkpoint persistence can still fail before that message is saved or published ([agent_runner_service.js](/C:/Users/janbo/Documents/dev/md2_workers/dev3/desktop/src/actions/agent/agent_runner_service.js:139)). The frontend has already cleared the draft, and `failSubmission` only marks the temporary row failed ([action_popup_operations.ts](/C:/Users/janbo/Documents/dev/md2_workers/dev3/app/src/components/actions/run/popup/action_popup_operations.ts:226), [action_conversation_store.ts](/C:/Users/janbo/Documents/dev/md2_workers/dev3/app/src/components/actions/conversation/state/action_conversation_store.ts:169)).

Yes. A queued message has a **Delete queued prompt** button. Deleting it emits `agentPromptRemoved` ([action_run.js](/C:/Users/janbo/Documents/dev/md2_workers/dev3/desktop/src/actions/action/action_run.js:146)).

The same event also fires when the backend takes a prompt out of the queue to send it. The frontend currently treats every removal as “wait for the sent message” ([action_conversation_store.ts](/C:/Users/janbo/Documents/dev/md2_workers/dev3/app/src/components/actions/conversation/state/action_conversation_store.ts:239)). The popup where Delete was clicked clears its own pending row through a separate callback; another open popup does not receive that callback, so it can show a false pending row.

The fix is to include the removal reason in the backend event, so every popup can clear a **deleted** prompt while retaining a **dispatching** prompt until its sent message arrives.

We have IDs, but they identify **which submission** is involved, not **why it left the queue**. The queued prompt has a `promptId`; the eventual sent message gets a different message ID and carries the local `submissionId`. A deleted prompt never produces that sent message.

I agree that `agentPromptRemoved` carries two meanings. The cleaner fix is separate events for **deleted**, **dispatched**, and **discarded** prompts, each carrying the queued prompt ID. Then every popup can clear deleted or discarded rows immediately and keep a dispatched row until its matching sent message arrives.

over complexity and bad design. we are duplicating ids and then creating yet other sets of ids to link everything together. waw. talk about over engineering.

simplify this.

> an ID alone cannot say whether a queued prompt was deleted or dispatched.

what are you talking about. this makes no sense. who ever said anything about only sending an id?

You’re right: the event can state what happened. I’ll replace the ambiguous removal event with explicit outcomes and trace the IDs through submission, queueing, and message persistence before changing that flow.

entries.content:
I simplified the prompt flow. The ID created for a frontend submission now stays with it as the queued prompt ID and, if sent, the persisted user message ID. The extra queue-to-submission link is gone.

The backend now emits distinct **deleted**, **dispatched**, and **discarded** events. Deletion clears the pending row in every popup through the shared event; dispatch keeps it visible until the message arrives.

Focused service tests, typecheck, and both linters pass. The popup test file still has two unrelated failures concerning usage display and a waiting-state button. I left the Git commit behavior unchanged.
